sites.reason:
claude-sonnet-4-6: removed TS2724; no new diagnostics. In Zod v4, `ZodType` no longer takes a definition type parameter — the signature changed from `ZodType<Output, Def extends ZodTypeDef, Input>` to `ZodType<Output, Input>`. `ZodTypeDef` is no longer exported. The fix is to:
1. Remove `ZodTypeDef` from the import (leaving only `ZodType`, or dropping the import entirely if `ZodType` is still used).
2. Replace `ZodType<TMessage, ZodTypeDef, unknown>` with `ZodType<TMessage, unknown>` in the constructor signature, preserving the same Output/Input contract without weakening types to `any`.

The `unknown` input type is kept so that the schema still validates arbitrary unknown input before narrowing to `TMessage`, which preserves the original validation intent.

attempts.explanation:
In Zod v4, `ZodType` no longer takes a definition type parameter — the signature changed from `ZodType<Output, Def extends ZodTypeDef, Input>` to `ZodType<Output, Input>`. `ZodTypeDef` is no longer exported. The fix is to:
1. Remove `ZodTypeDef` from the import (leaving only `ZodType`, or dropping the import entirely if `ZodType` is still used).
2. Replace `ZodType<TMessage, ZodTypeDef, unknown>` with `ZodType<TMessage, unknown>` in the constructor signature, preserving the same Output/Input contract without weakening types to `any`.

The `unknown` input type is kept so that the schema still validates arbitrary unknown input before narrowing to `TMessage`, which preserves the original validation intent.

sites.reason: claude-sonnet-4-6: removed TS2339; no new diagnostics. The `ZodString#ip()` method was removed in Zod 4. Per the migration guide, when the previous validator accepted both IPv4 and IPv6 (which is what the default `.ip()` with no version option did), the replacement is `z.union([z.ipv4(), z.ipv6()])`. These are now top-level factories rather than `z.string()` methods. No options or custom error text were passed in the original call, so no additional arguments need to be preserved.
